findings.statement: chunk verification pays on a skewed scan workload
findings.detail: Zipfian scans at 73655900 entries/s per chunk against 69407499 per block (chunk vs whole: greater 1.061x (p=0.0367, rel_iqr 1.9%/5.7%)). This is the regime chunking can help in at all: a uniform sweep reaches every chunk of every block it touches, and verifying all of a block's chunks is verifying the block

findings.statement: verifying a chunk instead of a block makes a cold scan cheaper
findings.detail: cold scans at 56349933 entries/s per chunk against 60063018 per block (chunk vs whole: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 0.938, p=0.6761) -- within noise, not a result)

findings.statement: the first pass now costs about what the steady state does
findings.detail: per chunk: 56349933 entries/s cold against 79377427 warm (1.41x). Per block: 60063018 against 81480700 (1.36x). f19-coldscan measured the whole-block ratio at 1.65x, and closing it is the point of this change -- a scan that has to warm up is a scan whose first pass is charged for every block it will ever touch

notes: one file, two readers, interleaved; the only difference is ReadOptions::chunk_verify
